title: Which preferences associate with school performance? – Lessons from a university exploratory study
author: Daniel Horn
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kepctdn

steps.title: Participant Registration and Setup
steps.instruction: Prepare participants for the experiment by ensuring anonymity and linking academic data.

substeps.instruction: Collect the participant's NEPTUN code to link experimental results with academic results (to be erased after linking).
Provide each participant with an answer sheet containing two identical number tags in the upper right corner.
Instruct participants to keep one tag and hand in the other with the completed answer sheet.

steps.title: Situation 1: Joint Account Contribution
steps.instruction: Conduct a contribution game where participants are randomly matched in pairs.

substeps.instruction: Assign an initial endowment of 4000 Ft to each participant.
Instruct participants to independently contribute any amount between 0 and 4000 Ft to a joint account.
Calculate final earnings as: (Initial endowment - contribution) + (70% of the total joint account contribution).

steps.title: Situation 2: Known Probability Bet
steps.instruction: Conduct a betting task with a known probability distribution.

substeps.instruction: Provide the participant with 3000 Ft.
Instruct the participant to place a bet between 0 and 3000 Ft on a color (red or black).
Draw one ball from a bag containing 10 black and 10 red balls.
If the drawn color matches the bet, double the bet amount; otherwise, the bet is lost.
Calculate final earnings as: (3000 - bet) + winnings from the bet.

steps.title: Situation 3: Unknown Probability Bet
steps.instruction: Conduct a betting task with an unknown probability distribution.

substeps.instruction: Provide the participant with 3000 Ft.
Instruct the participant to place a bet between 0 and 3000 Ft on a color (red or black).
Draw one ball from a bag containing an unknown number of black and red balls.
If the drawn color matches the bet, double the bet amount; otherwise, the bet is lost.
Calculate final earnings as: (3000 - bet) + winnings from the bet.

steps.title: Situation 4: Maze Solving
steps.instruction: Provide a maze for the participant to solve for an additional reward.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the participant to solve the provided maze.
Assign an additional 300 Ft if the maze is solved correctly and the participant is selected.

steps.title: Situation 5: Temporal Discounting (Short Term)
steps.instruction: Assess preference between immediate and delayed rewards (1 week).

substeps.instruction: Present a choice between a lower amount today or 3500 Ft in one week.
Instruct the participant to mark their preference for each row provided.

steps.title: Situation 6: Temporal Discounting (Long Term)
steps.instruction: Assess preference between delayed rewards (2 vs 3 weeks).

substeps.instruction: Present a choice between a given amount in two weeks or 3500 Ft in three weeks.
Instruct the participant to mark their preference for each row provided.

steps.title: Situation 7: Quiz and Compensation Choice
steps.instruction: Administer a general knowledge quiz and allow participants to choose their payment scheme.

substeps.instruction: Administer a quiz of 8 questions (covering logic, science, humanities, and general knowledge) without external help.
Ask the participant to guess how many questions they answered correctly.
Offer two compensation schemes:
Scheme A: 250 Ft for each correct answer.
Scheme B: Randomly pair with two other participants; if the participant has the highest number of correct answers, they receive 4500 Ft (2500 Ft in case of a tie); otherwise, 0 Ft.
Award an extra 250 Ft if the participant correctly guessed their number of correct answers.

steps.title: Final Selection and Payout
steps.instruction: Determine the final earnings for selected participants.

substeps.instruction: Collect all answer sheets.
Randomly select two participants based on the number tags.
Use a die to randomly select one of the six situations to determine the payout.
Pay the earnings immediately or according to the timeline specified in the chosen situation (1, 2, or 3 weeks).
For delayed payments, place the money in a sealed envelope to be delivered by the professor or collected at the Department of Economics (E3.59).
